trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out right or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2); going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,2). So the line goes down.
The line must go down: left is number 9, which comes later; right is number 4, which comes later.
Going left would force the line onto number 9 before its turn; going down, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 3. So the line goes right.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going down would leave both cell (6,4) and cell (6,6) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
Going up would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Going left would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (1,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going down would leave both cell (3,5) and number 7 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Cell (5,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Cell (2,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
